document.title: Exelon answers PJM’s request for more time on its capacity-auction complaint

MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER AND ANSWER OF  
EXELON CORPORATION    
Pursuant to Rules 2121 and 2132 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s 
(“Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedure, Exelon Corporation (“Exelon”) submits this 
motion for leave to answer and answer (“Answer”) to PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.’s (“PJM”) 
November 4, 2026, Preliminary Answer Opposing Fast-Track Processing and Motion for 
Extension of Time to Answer.3   
I. 
MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER 
While Rule 213(a)(3) permits answers to motions, the PJM Motion is simultaneously styled 
as a “preliminary” answer.  Though this designation clouds the procedural posture of the PJM 
Motion, out of an abundance of caution Exelon respectfully moves pursuant to Rule 212 for leave 
 
1 18 C.F.R. § 385.212. 
2 18 C.F.R. § 385.213(a)(3) (“An answer may be made to any pleading, if not prohibited under paragraph (a)(2) of 
this section.”).  Exelon submits this answer to the Motion component of PJM’s pleading, and accordingly an answer 
is permitted under Rule 213(a)(3).  To the extent that the Commission deems a motion necessary to process Exelon’s 
response to the “preliminary answer” component of PJM’s submission, Exelon respectfully moves for permission to 
respond, pursuant to Rule 212, as discussed herein. 
3 Exelon Corporation v. PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Preliminary Answer of PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. Opposing 
Fast-Track Processing and Motion for Extension of Time to Answer, Docket No. EL27-11-000 (Nov. 4, 2026) (“PJM 
Motion”).

2 
to answer.  While an answer to an answer or protest is not a matter of right under the Commission’s 
regulations,4 the Commission routinely permits such answers when the answer provides useful and 
relevant information that will assist the Commission in its decision-making process,5 corrects 
factual inaccuracies and clarifies the issues,6 provides information helpful to the disposition of an 
issue,7 or permits the issues to be narrowed.8  This Answer will assist the Commission in its 
decision-making process, clarifies the issues, and provides information helpful to the disposition 
of an issue.  Accordingly, Exelon respectfully requests the Commission grant leave and accept this 
Answer into the record of this proceeding. 
II. 
ANSWER 
A. Exelon Supports an Extension of the Comment Period to December 7, 2026. 
The default comment period for this complaint proceeding is twenty days under Rule 
206(f),9 or until November 23, 2026.  In justifying its extension request through December 21, 
2026, PJM states that “[t]he PJM Board is scheduled to consider these very issues at its November 
17, 2026 meeting, and the PJM Board’s determinations are expected to substantially inform PJM’s 
position regarding the issues raised in the Complaint.”10  PJM further explains that, “following the 
 
4 18 C.F.R. § 385.213(a)(2).  
5 See, e.g., Pioneer Transmission, LLC v. N. Ind. Pub. Serv. Co. and Midwest Indep. Transmission Sys. Operator, Inc., 
140 FERC ¶ 61,057, at P 94 (2012); Sw. Power Pool, Inc., 131 FERC ¶ 61,252, at P 19 (2010), reh’g denied, 137 
FERC ¶ 61,075 (2011) (accepting answers that “provided information that assisted us in our decision-making 
process”); Duke Energy Ky., Inc., 122 FERC ¶ 61,182, at P 25 (2008) (accepting answers to a protest that “provided 
information that assisted us in our decision-making process”); Tallgrass Transmission, LLC, 125 FERC ¶ 61,248, at 
P 26 (2008), reh’g denied, 150 FERC ¶ 61,224 (2015); PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 120 FERC ¶ 61,083, at P 23 
(2007) (answer to protests permitted when it provides information to assist the Commission in its decision-making 
process); Entergy Servs. Inc., 126 FERC ¶ 61,227, at P 76 (2009).  
6 See, e.g., PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 84 FERC ¶ 61,224, at 62,078 (1998).   
7 See, e.g., CNG Transmission Corp., 89 FERC ¶ 61,100, at 61,287, n.11 (1999).  
8 See, e.g., New Energy Ventures, Inc. v. S. Cal. Edison Co., 82 FERC ¶ 61,335, at 62,323, n.1 (1998). 
9 18 C.F.R. § 385.206(f) (“Unless otherwise ordered by the Commission, answers, interventions, and comments to a 
complaint must be filed within 20 days after the complaint is filed.”). 
10 PJM Motion at 5.

3 
PJM Board’s deliberations, PJM anticipates providing a timeline that outlines the stakeholder 
process through which a comprehensive package of capacity market enhancements, along with 
any associated filing(s), will be developed and finalized in PJM’s forthcoming answer.”11  
Exelon understands and appreciates the need for the PJM Board to deliberate and consider 
how PJM should respond to the instant complaint, and is amenable to providing PJM additional 
time.  However, the scale of PJM’s proposed extension is excessive for the narrow scope of the 
allegations it must answer.  PJM requests 28 days in addition to the default 20 days.  While PJM’s 
approach to a future “comprehensive package of capacity market enhancements” is certainly of 
interest, it is simply not what PJM must respond to in this docket.  The only legal question PJM is 
required to respond to in its answer is correspondingly the only legal question presented in the 
complaint: based on the evidence presented, has the three-year forward period of the Base Residual 
Auction (“BRA”)12 become unjust and unreasonable under the Federal Power Act (“FPA”) and, if 
so, whether a “prompt” auction schedule is a just and reasonable replacement rate.  As the 
established market administrator for decades, and during a period of time in which it has for 
months (or years) been deeply considering the current market shortcomings and needed remedies, 
it should not take PJM 48 days to express its opinion on this narrow legal question. Nor does PJM 
need to, in its answer, present a comprehensive road map of future stakeholder meetings and 
theoretical proposed enhancements to the Reliability Pricing Model (“RPM”).  While Exelon has 
 
11 Id. 
12 Terms not otherwise defined herein shall have the same meaning as set forth in the PJM Open Access Transmission 
Tariff (“Tariff”), the Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“Operating 
Agreement”), and the Reliability Assurance Agreement Among Load-Serving Entities in the PJM Region (“RAA”).  
The Tariff, Operating Agreement, and RAA are currently located under PJM’s “Intra-PJM Tariffs” eTariff title, 
available here: https://etariff.ferc.gov/TariffBrowser.aspx?tid=1731.

4 
already acknowledged such reforms will be necessary to “heal all that ails RPM”13 in the coming 
years, these future reforms are not within the scope of this narrow complaint proceeding, and PJM 
is not required to address them now. 
Furthermore, the PJM Motion provides no explanation as to why the PJM Board could not 
convene sooner to consider the limited issue raised in the complaint and provide the direction 
necessary for PJM to submit a timely answer within the comment period prescribed by the 
Commission’s regulations.  Nonetheless, Exelon supports an extension of the comment period 
until December 7, 2026, which will provide PJM with a total of 34 days after Exelon filed the 
complaint, and nearly three weeks after the PJM Board’s scheduled deliberations conclude on 
November 17, 2026.  Exelon submits that this date strikes a reasonable balance between PJM’s 
request for additional time and the exigency of Commission action sufficiently in advance of the 
May 2027 BRA, as discussed below in Section II.B. 
B. Exelon Urges the Commission to Act Sufficiently in Advance of the May 2027 
BRA. 
Exelon takes no position in this Answer regarding PJM’s analysis as to when legal 
consequence attaches to a Commission-jurisdictional auction process, and in many ways this is 
beside the point.  Rule 206(h) does not specify a fixed temporal deadline for a Commission 
decision on the merits of a complaint requesting fast-track processing, and provides the 
Commission with broad discretion in how to act.14  Whatever the action date the Commission 
ultimately selects, Exelon respectfully requests the Commission issue its order sufficiently in 
 
13 Exelon Corp. v. PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Complaint Requesting Fast-Track Processing of Exelon Corporation 
at 6, Docket No. EL27-11-000 (Nov. 3, 2026). 
14 18 C.F.R. § 385.206(h)(1) (“The Commission may resolve complaints using Fast Track procedures if the complaint 
requires expeditious resolution.  Fast Track procedures may include expedited action on the pleadings by the 
Commission, expedited hearing before an ALJ, or expedited action on requests for stay, extension of time, or other 
relief by the Commission or an ALJ.”).

5 
advance of the May 2027 BRA.  The primary issue presented in this proceeding—the lawfulness 
of the three-year forward period of the BRA—is of critical importance to Market Participants 
across the PJM Region.  Irrespective of when the consequence of Commission inaction will attach 
legally, it will certainly attach practically, as parties try to position themselves sufficiently in 
advance of the uncapped surge in capacity prices coming this May.  Moreover, establishment of a 
refund effective date is not a substitute for timely Commission action: the relief Exelon seeks is 
prospective, and it can be meaningfully provided only before the auction process moves forward.15  
Accordingly, Exelon urges the Commission to act expeditiously in this proceeding. 
III. 
CONCLUSION 
For these reasons, Exelon requests the Commission establish an extended comment date of 
December 7, 2026, and consider expeditiously the instant complaint so the Commission can act 
sufficiently in advance of the May 2027 BRA. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Respectfully submitted,

15 PJM suggests that establishing a refund effective date preserves any remedy, so expedited action is unnecessary.  
PJM Motion at 3, 8–10.  As a practical matter, it does not.  PJM acknowledges that the Commission has historically 
been reluctant to order refunds related to final market results, and that PJM has opposed such requests.  Id. at 9.  It 
would presumably do so again.  Any after-the-fact remedy would require unwinding or re-pricing auction results that 
Market Participants have already relied on, which is the outcome PJM itself says it has resisted.
